name: Jake Hansen
current_role: Co-founder, CompanyCam (Lincoln, Nebraska); formerly COO of family business White Castle Roofing
profile: One of the Hansen brothers from Lincoln, Nebraska's White Castle Roofing (founded by father Mike Hansen in 1985) who co-founded CompanyCam in 2015, a photo-documentation app for contractors. Brother Luke Hansen is CEO; CompanyCam was valued at about $2B in 2025.
interesting_fact: CompanyCam began as an in-house fix for the Hansens' own roofing company, whose job-site photos were scattered across files and drives with no way to sort them by time, date and address.
deep_cut_fact: As COO of White Castle Roofing, Jake focused on quality control and shot before-and-after photos of jobs with a DSLR, the photo habit that later inspired CompanyCam.
notes: Low public profile; Luke Hansen (CEO) is the public face. The founders story uses only 'Jake'. A CompanyCam blog post says Mike Hansen's youngest son Jacob runs White Castle Roofing in Omaha (https://companycam.com/blog/mike-hansen-roofing-advice), so Jake may be focused on the roofing business. Best route: via CompanyCam press.

name: Edward Woodford
profile: UK-born (Spanish/English background) founder who moved to the US for graduate school at MIT and co-founded zerohash, crypto and stablecoin infrastructure-as-a-service for brokerages and fintechs. In early 2026 he turned down a reported $2B acquisition offer from Mastercard, and zerohash has since applied for a US national trust bank charter.
interesting_fact: He turned down a roughly $2B acquisition offer from Mastercard in early 2026, saying zerohash could grow more in the next two years than in its first eight.
deep_cut_fact: He says rejection from Oxford was 'the best thing' for him because it pushed him to MIT, where a class with Christian Catalini got him into Bitcoin and he bought his first Bitcoin at the MIT bookstore. He also wrote a children's book, 'Stable Coins for Babies', which he gives to expecting friends.
notes: Very media-active (podcasts, Semafor, Consensus, WEF author page); responsive to fintech press. Earlier co-founded Seed CX per secondary sources (not verified).

name: Jeremy De Groodt
profile: Belgian engineer who co-founded Keyrock in Brussels in 2017 with Kevin de Patoul and Juan David Mendieta. Keyrock is an algorithmic market maker and liquidity provider for digital assets, valued at about $1.1B in 2026. Before Keyrock he led software teams building secure applications for European institutions and banks, and he oversees Keyrock's technical infrastructure.
interesting_fact: Forbes Belgium calls Keyrock Belgium's first crypto unicorn, valued at about $1.1B after a 2026 funding round; De Groodt built its algorithmic trading infrastructure from scratch.
deep_cut_fact: He made Rust the foundation of Keyrock's trading systems and promotes 'RustFi'. He has said the Rust learning curve is 'as steep as El Capitan', and Keyrock hosted a RustFi hackathon in Berlin in 2022 with a EUR 100,000 prize pool.
notes: Technical co-founder with a low profile; CEO Kevin de Patoul does most press. The press email belongs to Keyrock's PR and Events Manager (Marina Sanchez), the media contact named in the July 2026 press release.

name: Zach Maurides
profile: Former Duke football offensive lineman who began building scheduling and communication software for Duke athletic teams while a student. He launched Teamworks full-time in 2010 with Shaun Powell and Mitch Heath. Teamworks is now an operating platform used by thousands of college and pro teams, grown through acquisitions such as INFLCR and Smartabase, and valued at about $1B.
interesting_fact: Teamworks started from a Duke class project in which Maurides, a sophomore offensive guard juggling athletics and classes, was asked to design software that would improve his own life.
deep_cut_fact: In a Duke essay he wrote that in college he 'played for four offensive coordinators, three position coaches and two head coaches', and that the variety of leadership styles shaped him as a young entrepreneur.
notes: Sports Business Journal Forty Under 40 honoree; appears on sports-business podcasts. Best route: Teamworks PR.
